reason: The text contains multiple explicit instances where the Hebrew people blame Moses and Aaron for putting them at risk. In Exodus 14:11-12, after seeing the pursuing Egyptians, the people ask why they were taken from Egypt, expressing that they would have preferred to remain enslaved. In Exodus 16:2-3, they complain about hunger and wish they had died in Egypt. In Exodus 17:3, they accuse Moses of bringing them into the wilderness to die of thirst. These passages demonstrate that the Israelites hold their leaders responsible for the hardships and dangers they face during the exodus journey.
